Compose Multiplatform, one screen from state to pixels · check

Know One screen, two platforms already?

One question for each of the 4 puzzles in this module. A right answer marks that puzzle as passed, so you can jump ahead. A wrong one tells you which puzzle to start with. Nothing is sent anywhere: it's saved in this browser.

Puzzle 6: Who read the bookmark count?

The screen reads count.value and passes the number to the header. A tap changes the count. Which group does Compose mark?

Right. The read decides which group is marked.

Not quite. A write marks only the groups that read the value. Learn it in puzzle 6 →

Not quite. Compose follows where the read happened, not where the value is shown. Learn it in puzzle 6 →

Puzzle 7: Which work does a moving card need?

The card now also grows taller as you scroll, and its height follows the same position. Can placement alone handle that change?

Not quite. The offset lambda only moves the card; a height change has to be measured. Learn it in puzzle 7 →

Right. Size changes need measuring; position changes don't.

Not quite. Drawing paints what layout decided; it doesn't choose sizes. Learn it in puzzle 7 →

Puzzle 8: Which side hosts the other?

An existing UIKit navigation controller must present a shared screen. Which object belongs in its screen stack?

Not quite. The host needs an iOS controller that contains the shared UI. Learn it in puzzle 8 →

Not quite. UIKitView embeds a native view in the other direction. Learn it in puzzle 8 →

Right. Start from whoever owns the surrounding region.

Puzzle 9: Can VoiceOver understand the bookmark?

The icon is solid after saving, but the action has no label or state. What is the missing signal?

Not quite. Changing pixels does not expose a saved state to the screen reader. Learn it in puzzle 9 →

Right. Provide the meaning of the control along with its pixels.

Not quite. The navigation bar does not describe an unlabeled bookmark. Learn it in puzzle 9 →
